name: Kryovast
geological_features: Glacial plains extending unbroken for thousands of kilometers
Cryovolcanic vents erupting slurries of ammonia and water ice
Subsurface ocean detected beneath a sixty-kilometer ice shell
Pressure ridges forming labyrinthine ice walls at tectonic boundaries
specific_features: A vast, perfectly smooth frozen plain nicknamed the Mirror, reflecting starlight with eerie clarity
Deep crevasse networks that reveal blue-green ice layers hundreds of meters below the surface
description: Kryovast is a world locked in deep freeze, its entire surface entombed beneath kilometers of ancient ice that has not seen liquid water on its surface in eons. The terrain alternates between vast, featureless plains of wind-polished ice and chaotic zones where tectonic stress has shattered the crust into towering pressure ridges.

The thin atmosphere offers little insulation or protection, allowing temperatures to plunge to nearly two hundred degrees below zero during the long polar nights. What air exists carries fine ice crystals that catch distant starlight, creating shimmering halos and phantom pillars of luminescence on the horizon.

Seismic surveys have confirmed the existence of a liquid water ocean some sixty kilometers beneath the frozen surface, kept warm by tidal heating from the planet's gravitational interaction with its parent star. Cryovolcanic activity periodically breaches the ice shell, ejecting plumes of briny slush that freeze into towering formations before collapsing under their own weight.

Kryovast's subsurface ocean represents a tantalizing target for deep-drilling exploration missions, though the sheer depth of the ice shell presents formidable engineering challenges. The surface ice itself contains substantial water reserves valuable for fuel synthesis, and the planet's isolation makes it an ideal candidate for long-term research installations far from contested space lanes.
